Part 1 · The six stages

What does a team do between “something is wrong” and “it is fixed”?

Part 1 · the plan

A method that slows the jump to a cause

  1. Why a methodthe trap of naming a cause first
  2. Problem, Review and six stagesthe question and the deliverable of each
  3. Fact, inference, opinionsorting what the team is told
  4. Is it time-critical?run, safe-park or shut down, before diagnosing
  5. Hypotheses that can dieevery cause written so a test can kill it

Why a method

The fastest diagnosis is often the wrong one

The trap

Name a cause at the first symptom, then look only for support.

Facts first

Record what was seen, by whom, when, with numbers.

Causes must die

Write each cause as a prediction a safe test can refute.

After Woods: a Problem record, a Review of fundamentals, then six stages.

Interactive · step through the stages

Each stage asks one question and delivers one thing

    Stage 0 forbids causes; causes enter only at Explore, after urgency and a testable problem statement.

    Interactive · sort each statement

    Fact, inference or opinion?

    Your sorting

    An inference is computed from facts; an opinion waits in a separate list until a test verifies it.

    Statements from the TE-1 worked example (stages 1.2, 3.1, 3.7 and the evidence list).

    Interactive · Engage, before any diagnosis

    Run, safe-park or shut down?

    TE-1 sits inside its alarms and is falling: keep running and investigate. Near a limit and rising: safe-park first.

    Limits: TI-224 HI 285, TSHH trip 300 °C; PIC-203 HI 78, PSHH trip 85, PSV-201 88 bar g. Safe-park = a reduced, stable state.

    Explore · the working hypothesis

    Write every cause so a test can kill it

    Ifthe bed 1 exit thermocouple TE-214 reads low,
    thenonly TI-214 moves and its spare element disagrees;
    it dies ifthe spare equals TI-214 or other tags moved too.

    Working hypothesis WH-8 of the TE-1 example. Each is scored P × S × T: probability, severity, testability (1–5).

    Part 1 · summary

    What part 1 settled

    • Problem and Review, then Engage, Define, Explore, Plan, Do it, Look back.
    • Facts, inferences and opinions are kept apart.
    • Urgency is decided before the diagnosis starts.
    • Each cause carries a prediction and a falsifier.

    Part 2 · Workbook and OTS

    How does the workbook work with the running simulator?

    Part 2 · the plan

    One tab, one workbook, one simulator

    1. The tab and its six stepsfrom loading a case to the report
    2. Three live pullsrun data, unit snapshot and event log, no files
    3. Record time and OTS timewhy a case can start an hour earlier
    4. The stage pageswhat each stage looks like when filled
    5. Tests on the OTSfive kinds of action, five gates before a move

    Systematic problem solving tab

    The workbook runs inside the OTS page

    1. Load a TE case in Exercises and the workbook
    2. Run 10–20 min, touch nothing
    3. Pull all three data sets
    4. Work the stages 0 to 6
    5. Test on the OTS, pull again
    6. Report: Word, slides, project file

    Interactive · OTS data & evidence ▸ Pull all three

    Three pulls from the running simulator

    The workbook reads the simulator directly; fault and instructor lines never reach a trainee's log.

    Interactive · two clocks

    Record time starts at the case's history

    Pulled data carry times. A case with a history needs two clocks.

    TE-1 hands over after an hour of drift: record 1:00:00 = OTS 0:00:00, so the workbook shows no negative times.

    Plan · stage 4

    Five kinds of action, five gates before a move

    Diagnostic actions

    1. decide NOT to do
    2. quick action
    3. stop the rapid change
    4. others collect information
    5. plant experiment

    Gates

    1. safe-park done or not needed
    2. everyone affected told
    3. stop criteria as numbers
    4. who may stop it
    5. way back written

    Part 2 · summary

    What part 2 settled

    • Load, run, pull, work the stages, test, report.
    • Run data, snapshot and event log come straight from the OTS.
    • Record time starts with the case's history.
    • No plant test without its five gates.

    Interactive · Define · IS / IS NOT

    Where the problem is, and where it is not

    Engage found nothing near a limit: keep running. Now pin the problem down.

    IS

    IS NOT

    So it is not

    Every bed shifted together and CH₄ fell: not a local loss, not an inert build-up.

    Interactive · Define · desired final state

    Is the goal SMARTS-$?

    Only D names numbers, a deadline, a safety limit and a cost, and accepts what cannot be restored on line.

    Interactive · Explore → Plan → Do it

    Eight hypotheses, two tests, one survivor

    The cheap look-and-ask round killed four causes without touching the process; one small move settled the last two.

    Interactive · test T-2 · TIC-211 SP 220 → 227 °C at 1:20:02

    Is the bed 1 catalyst dead or only slow?

    Kill criterion, written before the move: bed 1 ΔT grows by more than 3 °C → WH-2 (dead zone) killed, WH-1 (slow catalyst) confirmed.

    +6.8 °C at the inlet gave +14.2 °C at the exit: the catalyst is alive but slow, aged in every bed.

    Do it · 1:40:00 · circulation +10 %, bed 2/3 inlets +5 °C

    The fix against its prediction

    After 30 minPredictedActual
    XI-210 methanol, t/habout +1+1.03
    FI-203 purge, kNm³/habout −3−2.4
    AI-205 CO, %about −0.3−0.33
    JI-201 C-201 power, MWabout +2+2.12

    A third of the 3.3 t/h lost: lost activity is only partly compensated. The real fix is the catalyst change.

    Look back · stage 6

    Will it stay fixed, and what changes next time?

    Rule for next shift

    High purge, steady make-up: read the bed ΔTs before blaming the front end.

    Sustain

    Trend bed 1 ΔT weekly; plan the change below ≈ 20 °C.

    New problem

    C-201 at 88 % speed; hotter inlets age the catalyst faster.

    Part 3 · summary

    What part 3 settled

    • Purge up, methanol down, feeds on set point: the converter converts less.
    • IS / IS NOT ruled out a local loss and inerts.
    • T-1 killed four causes; T-2 confirmed catalyst ageing.
    • Compensation won back a third; plan the catalyst change.

    This deck

    Key Takeaways

    1

    Record facts with numbers before naming any cause.

    2

    Decide urgency first: run, safe-park or shut down.

    3

    Write each cause with the observation that would kill it.

    4

    Kill cheap hypotheses by looking before changing the plant.

    5

    Compare the fix with its prediction, then write the rule.
